## Installing R

This workshop is based in the [R programming language](https://www.r-project.org/){target="_blank"}. 
As such, it is necessary to have a recent version installed on your computer. I would suggest R Version $\geq$ 4.4. 

These workshop materials were built and tested using R version 4.6.1 (Happy Hop, released 2026-06-26), with all packages updated on or after Septmber 14, 2026.

## Installing R Studio Desktop

[Posit](https://posit.co/){target="_blank"} makes a wonderful integrated development environment (IDE) called [R Studio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/){target="_blank"}. 
This _was_ my preferred IDE for R; I've since starting using VS Code because my organization offers an LLM coding assistant through that IDE.  
I will be using R Studio throughout the workshop, except for a brief demonstration of how LLM coding assistants work.
Posit also makes [Positron], which is largely based on VS Code, and will be their primary IDE going forward.

I am using R Studio Version 2026.01.2+418, which was installed on September 14, 2026. Newer versions are available to use; I am required to use this version by my organization.

## Installing R Tools

[RTools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/){target="_blank"} is necessary to install or build R packages that require compilation of C, C++, or Fortran code, as it provides the necessary compiler toolchain and build tools. 
The packages that are available on [CRAN](https://cran.rstudio.com/){target="_blank"} do not require having RTools installed because the packages hosted there are precompiled binary packages.

I'm unsure of which packages I've downloaded from Github or other sources that require compilation, so I recommend also installing at RTools 4.5 or newer. I'm using 4.5.6768.
(And it's just good to have in case you need it later.)
